mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a FEDFUNDS increase > 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and economic growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a UNRATE increase > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances following two consecutive quarters of declining GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves and economic growth prospects rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances following a INDPRO increase > 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls by more than 100,000 in a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a PAYEMS decrease > 100,000.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and a decrease in retail sales signal a shift in consumer spending from goods to housing, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the market anticipates increased demand in the housing sector.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases & RSAFS decreases in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a simultaneous increase in HOUST and decrease in RSAFS.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the consumer price index by more than 0.5% in a month signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the market anticipates tighter monetary policy and reduced consumer purchasing power.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales over two consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised upwards.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances following two consecutive months of increasing RSAFS.
